chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Dick Gibson's party in Vail
summary: Gus describes arriving in Vail, playing with Teddy Wilson, Milt Hinton and others, and being asked back.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: You hit it off with Dick.
He called me after Jack got finished talking. He called me later, and he told me the same thing Jack had just told me, see.
Yeah.
So I told him, 'Yeah, I'll make it, be happy to make it.' And so I came out, and I played the party, which was set at Vail, Colorado.
Yeah, before they moved it.
Yeah. The first one before then was in Aspen.
Yeah.
But this time it was in Vail. So I got here and met everybody, a lot of my friends from New York and different places. Surprised, to see them all --
To see who's there.
Yeah. Which I was happy that I was there, too.
Sure, that's right.

And so he made out the slip. He said, 'I don't know, maybe you'll get to play, like I said. But don't worry about it, you'll get your money anyway.' I said, 'Well, that's okay. If I play, I play. If I don't, I don't.' Because I knew I was going to enjoy myself, like that.
Yeah.
And so he put me up in one of the
rooms in one of his houses. He had four houses then.
Yeah.
And so we went to Vail and I was listening to the guys, different ones, playing, Teddy Wilson --
Joe Venuti.
Yeah, Joe Venuti. And Milt Hinton was there, and Bob Haggert. They had what they called the giants of jazz, the great giants of jazz.
Yeah.
So -- but Billy Butterfield, a lot of the -- Safransky on bass.
Yeah.
He was my roommate.
Oh, was he?
Yeah. And he didn't make it that night because of the altitude. Safranski. He got very sick.
Is that right?
But it ended up, I played with Teddy Wilson and Milt Hinton, just like that.
Oh, sure.
And everybody loved it, see. And so I've been making it ever since.
The thing was -- I guess Dick realized that you could fall in follow behind anybody, really, more or less.
